MISSION VIEJO MINUTES
  City Council, Community Development Financing Authority,
  Successor Agency of the Community Development Agency,
  Housing Authority, and Library Board of Trustees*

  August 26, 2025
A Regular Meeting of the City Council, the Community Development Financing Authority, the
Successor Agency of the Community Development Agency, the Housing Authority, and the Library
Board of Trustees of the City of Mission Viejo, California, was called to order by Mayor Ruesch at
5:00 p.m., on August 26, 2025, at 200 Civic Center, Mission Viejo, California.

A complete copy of the agenda for the meeting containing all items as shown herein was posted by
5:00 p.m. on August 21, 2025, on the outdoor bulletin board at City Hall. A copy was also posted
at the Montanoso Recreation and Fitness Center, 25800 Montanoso Drive and Norman P. Murray
Community and Senior Center, 24932 Veterans Way.

*All Board and Agency memberships are reflected in the title "Council Member."

Present:  Council Member Goodell
  Council Member Kelley
  Council Member Vasquez
  Mayor Ruesch

Absent:  Mayor Pro Tem Bucknum

Staff Present:  Elaine Lister, City Manager
  Jerry Hill, Assistant City Manager
  William P. Curley, City Attorney
  Ellis Chang, Director of Administrative Services
  Kimberly Schmitt, City Clerk
  Renata Winter, Assistant City Clerk

  Negotiations Are the City and City’s Unrepresented Employees. The City’s Negotiator
  is Elaine Lister

CS2. Conference with Real Property Negotiators: Property Los Osos, 25282 Marguerite

City Council Minutes  1  August 26, 2025

RECESS TO CLOSED SESSION AND RECONVENE

At the hour of 5:00 pm Mayor Ruesch recessed the meeting to Closed Session. Mayor Ruesch
reconvened the meeting at 6:07pm with four City Council Members present.

REPORT OF CLOSED SESSION

City Attorney Curley announced that there were three closed session items, labor negotiations, real
estate property negotiations, and existing litigation. Council was updated, but no reportable actions
occurred.

INVOCATION: Council Member Vasquez

PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE: Council Member Kelley

PRESENTATIONS

P1. Proclaim September 2025 To Be National Service Dog Month

  Mayor Ruesch presented the proclamation to Jan Heppert.

P2. Mission Viejo BBQ Music Fest Update

Tom Moore, M.V.: Commented on the event that he is supportive of it, however some of his
neighbors were not due to the noise levels. He asked how much of the ten dollar parking charge
was allotted to youth athletics.

  Received update from Recreation and Community Services Director Mark Nix.

P3. Photo Contest Winner Announcement

  Mayor Ruesch announced that the winner of the photo contest is James Castillo.

PUBLIC COMMENTS

Tom Moore, M.V.: Asked what the cost to the city through 2024 is for the 2007 ULI Village
Center Study and the 2017 Village Center Study.

Isabelle Zhang, M.V.: Spoke on the Community of Character Trait for the month of August -Self
Control.

Karen Warren, M.V. and June Anderson, M.V.: Spoke on the lack of response from OCSD on the
calls regarding protestors at a forum being held at Casta del Sol.
City Council Minutes  2  August 26, 2025
 Nicolas Valencia, M.V.: Advocated for a ban on pesticides at Coronado Park and voiced his
concerns on the spraying of the sidewalks while children were playing in the park.

Randall Simmons, M.V.: Asked when the election dates for City Council positions will be
published and when the data from the surveillance cameras procedures be put in place to ensure
transparency. Lastly, asked for better control of toxic chemicals in the city and suggested the city
set aside financial assistance to those affected by ICE.

Police Chief Ivins responded to the two speakers regarding the protest at Casta del Sol. He
explained that there were deputies in the vicinity from approximately 2:00 pm to 4:30 pm to keep
the peace.

Assistant City Manager Jerry Hill commented that they did talk to the contractor regarding the
spraying and that it will not happen again. The employee was reprimanded.

Mayor Ruesch commented that the City Council Elections are November 3, 2026, and that has not
changed. Anyone that is interested can file the proper paperwork at any time. He announced that
the staggering of districts will be on the September 23 agenda.

MAYOR’S, COMMISSION, COMMITTEE REPORTS AND ACTIONS

24. Voting Delegate and Alternate(s) for the 2025 League of California Cities Annual

  By consensus Mayor Ruesch appointed himself as voting delegate and Council Member
  Kelley and Council Member Vasquez as alternates for the League of California Cities
  Conference Annual Business Meeting on Friday, October 10, 2025.

CITY MANAGER REPORTS

Assistant City Manager gave an update on the Fire Mitigation Grant from Cal Fire with tree
removals of declining eucalyptus trees along Vista Del Lago and some vegetation thinning along
the ridgeline area which is in the large open space surrounded by Vista Del Lago and Los Alisos
and Via Novena area. He indicated that an amendment was filed to the Cal Fire Grant relative to
the 100 feet defensible space limits requesting an additional 70 feet from housing structures in the
open space area which would be the homes behind Via Noveno and Via Santiago. He announced
that the amendment was approved last week and that the CEQA document will be adjusted. Another
grant was submitted to focus on the removal of palm trees with dead fronds in opens spaces along
with pampas grass and some of the non-natives along the Creek areas in the open space. The grant
also includes provisions for goat grazing as well. The grant we received was two million dollars
and the maximum amount of this grant is nine hundred and fifty thousand which we requested. The
goats will be in the area off Jeronimo between Silleros and Pavion in the open space between the
two trails. The contractor is working on a staging area this week and the goats will arrive after
Labor Day and we will do a press release with more information.

CITY ATTORNEY REPORTS

City Attorney Curly had no report.

COUNCIL MEMBER COMMENTS AND ACTIONS

25. Council Member Reports of Events and Activities Attended ~ AB1234

  By consensus, the City Council Members acknowledged their event and activities calendars
  as presented in the report and agreed to provide any changes to the City Clerk for the public

City Council Minutes  6  August 26, 2025
 Council Member Goodell

Council Member Goodell commented that the recent mileage and event report was notably
extensive, reflecting significant activity since our last meeting. A key highlight was the Junior
Nationals diving competition held in July at the Marguerite Aquatics Complex, which hosted over
300 divers and their families over a ten-day period. During the event’s opening ceremonies, the
dive well was dedicated in honor of Dr. Ron O’Brien, a distinguished coach who developed
numerous Olympians locally and nationally. Additionally, the regional Masters Swimming
Championships were held last weekend, featuring over 200 competitors ranging in age from 1 to
99. Of a particular note, Mary T. Meagher—known as “Madame Butterfly” from the 1984
Olympics—set a new world record in the 200-meter butterfly for the 61–64 age group and narrowly
missed breaking the 100-meter record. The Mayor, Council Member Vasquez, and Council
Member Goodell attended the grand opening and ribbon-cutting ceremony for Saddleback ATEP,
a state-of-the-art culinary and educational facility in Tustin. Lastly, he also had the opportunity to
attend an exceptional symphony performance, participate in a Chamber of Commerce mixer
involving four city chambers, and serve as a judge at the recent BBQ Fest.

Council Member Kelley

Council Member Kelley gave kudos to Director Mark nix and his team for the Barbecue Music Fest
which was held July 25 through July 27. She also attended the Junior National Dive Meet which
brought in a lot of people from all over the country. Council Member Kelley gave a shout out to
Chief Ivins and his crew for National Night Out which was held on July 31st and a successful event.
She gave kudos to City Manager Lister and Assistant City Manager Hill along with city staff for
the wonderful Prelude in the Park event. She encouraged residents to attend one of the night
markets at Los Oso which is every third Saturday of the month. Council Member Kelley also
attended the second time around jewelry sale fundraiser that was a huge success raising forty
thousand dollars that will go toward senior programs. She thanked Commissioner Josh Vechionne
for his participation in helping to appraise the jewelry, as well as the Senior Activities Committee
and Melanie McGrain for their great work in holding this event. Council Member Kelly attended
the Paddle for the Battle Pickleball Tournament that raised eight thousand dollars for the American
Cancer Society and thanked staff members Amanda and Tiffany at the Felipe Tennis Center for
their hard work. She announced that on September 20 at Oso Viejo Park will be the annual Relay
for Life from 1:00 pm until 9:00 pm. Lastly, she reminded residents that this coming Sunday August
31 the Marine Adoption Committee is hosting the Boots, Beer, and Barbecue event at the Norman
P. Community Center. The cost is thirty-five dollars per person, and the proceeds go to support the
marines and sailors of our adopted headquarters battalion.

Council Member Vasquez

Council Member Vasquez reported attending several community events recently. She participated
in the Station 24 ribbon cutting ceremony, noting that it was well attended and a great event. She
also enjoyed an outing to the symphony with family and friends, which was similarly well attended
and enjoyable. Additionally, Council Member Vasquez attended the Saddleback ATEP Grand
Opening and encouraged residents to explore the variety of classes offered through the program.
On a personal note, she recapped her summer, highlighting a memorable family cruise to Alaska.
She shared that her eldest daughter has started at Cal State Long Beach, while her youngest enjoyed

City Council Minutes  7  August 26, 2025
 a range of summer camps. The summer also included family birthday celebrations and attending
baseball games together.

Mayor Ruesch

Mayor Ruesch highlighted several key events and developments that took place in Mission Viejo
over the recent hiatus. He acknowledged Council Member Vasquez’s mention of the Station 24
Grand Opening and shared a video from the event. Reflecting on his involvement from the
beginning as a member of the design review committee alongside former Mayor Bob Breton, he
expressed pride in witnessing the project come to life. Now serving as the Mission Viejo
representative for OCFA, Mayor Ruesch attended the re-launch and described Station 24 as the
finest fire station OCFA has. He also shared his experience attending the local symphony and the
after-party, where food was served by the Oso Creek Golf Course, describing the event as
phenomenal. Additionally, Mayor Ruesch spoke about a memorable ceremony held in the Rotary
Garden, where the city dedicated a peace and mental health poll—the first known in the United
States as a place for reflection and understanding, recognizing the importance of mental health.
Finally, Mayor Ruesch expressed condolences on the passing of former employee Susan Knudson.
He honored her as an integral, well-respected, and dedicated member of the city staff who continued
to contribute even during her illness, notably helping to complete the city budget. He adjourned the
meeting in her memory.

ADJOURNMENT

At the hour of 7:18 p.m., with no further business to come before the City Council at this session,
Mayor Ruesch adjourned the meeting in memory of Administrative Services Manager Susan
Knudson to Tuesday September 9, 2025.
